samples.summary: `style.alignment` is interpolated unescaped and unvalidated into `<w:jc w:val="…">` — the same OOXML attribute-injection sink class this change hardens for colors, three lines below the fixed code
samples.evidence: buildParagraphPropertiesXml does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;` then `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` for anything that is not the literal 'left' (docx-style-map.ts:123-126). Unlike `fontFamily` (escaped at line 70-71) and now `color`/`backgroundColor` (normalized at 95/99), `align` gets neither escaping nor an allowlist. BlockStyle.alignment is typed as a closed union, but the runtime value comes from the Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` only spreads defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) — no validation anywhere on that path. Attack: a collaborator with write access to a shared doc (or anything writing the tree attr, incl. the backend docs-tree serializer) sets the block attribute `alignment` to `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` (or `a" w:x="`); when any other user exports the document, DocxExporter emits that string verbatim into word/document.xml (and header1.xml/footer1.xml via buildHeaderFooterXml), closing the `<w:jc>` element and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open in Word. Note the PPTX exporter does allowlist the same field (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79), which is the pattern missing here. Confidence is medium only because I could not confirm the Yorkie server accepts an arbitrary `alignment` attribute value from a peer client; the exporter-side sink itself is unambiguous.

samples.summary: Peer-supplied `peer.color` is interpolated into a CSS `style` attribute string for remote-selection decorations without validation (out of diff, same 'color string is untrusted' theme)
samples.evidence: `attributes: { style: `background-color: ${peer.color}` }` builds a style declaration from another collaborator's presence value; the same value is also assigned at lines 60-61. CodeMirror applies decoration attributes with setAttribute, so this is CSS injection rather than HTML injection — a peer can append extra declarations (e.g. `red; background-image: url(https://attacker/?t=…)`) to force outbound requests or spoof editor chrome for every other viewer. Untouched by this change and unrelated to #728; surfaced because it is the one remaining place a peer-controlled color string reaches a markup sink unvalidated. I did not verify how `peer.color` is populated in packages/notes/src/store/store.ts:33, hence low confidence.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. (1) The sink exists exactly as quoted: docx-style-map.ts:123-126 interpolates `align` into `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` with no escapeXmlAttr() and no allowlist; the `align !== 'left'` guard admits ANY non-'left' string, so it is not a validating check. This sits 20-30 lines below the escaped fontFamily path (:70-71) and the normalized color paths (:95, :99), confirming the same-file inconsistency. (2) An unvalidated runtime value can reach it: yorkie-doc-store.ts:220 does an unchecked cast `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` from a raw Record<string,string> of tree attributes, and normalizeBlockStyle (types.ts:272-274) only spreads defaults so a supplied value overrides verbatim; the union at types.ts:103 is compile-time only. (3) The value reaches files other users open: docx-exporter.ts:186-191 passes block.style into buildParagraphPropertiesXml and concatenates into <w:p>, and buildHeaderFooterXml (:109, :121, :360) does the same for header/footer parts. I searched for an upstream guard that would make this unreachable and found the opposite: only the DOCX import path allowlists alignment (import/docx-style-map.ts:104-107 with an else -> 'left' fallback), which covers imports but leaves the collaborative-tree path unvalidated. No refutation ground applies: not not-present (code is verbatim), not already-guarded (the only allowlist is on a different path), and unescaped attribute interpolation of untrusted input into an OOXML document opened by other users is squarely in the injection/unsafe-input-handling lane. The reviewer's own medium confidence concerns exploitability of the peer-write vector, not the reality of the missing escaping, and under this lens uncertainty keeps the finding.
